entities.name: Caspar Aquila
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Caspar Aquila (1488? – December 2, 1560), born Johann Kaspar Adler, was a pivotal German Lutheran theologian and reformer whose work profoundly shaped the nascent Protestant movement in Saxony and beyond during the critical decades of the 16th century. His steadfast adherence to Martin Luther's doctrines, particularly on justification by faith, positioned him as a key figure in consolidating the theological foundations of Lutheranism amidst intense religious and political upheaval. Serving as a pastor, superintendent, and professor, Aquila bridged the academic rigor of Wittenberg with the practical demands of church administration, contributing significantly to the establishment of Protestant ecclesiastical structures in central Germany.

Aquila's early life saw him studying in Leipzig, Wittenberg, and Rome, where he witnessed the corruption of the Catholic Church firsthand, fueling his eventual embrace of reformist ideals. After returning to Germany, he became a fervent supporter of Martin Luther, serving as a pastor in Jesterhausen (1515-1519) and then as a court chaplain to Franz von Sickingen. Imprisoned for his Lutheran sympathies in 1521, he was freed through the intervention of Sickingen and subsequently became a professor of Hebrew in Wittenberg in 1524, working closely with Luther and Philipp Melanchthon on the German Bible translation. His superintendency in Saalfeld (1527-1548) was marked by vigorous implementation of evangelical church orders, educational reforms, and a steadfast pastoral presence during the turbulent Schmalkaldic War (1546-1547).
